extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / scientists and scholars seeking methodological guidance for empirical research and the compilation of natural history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to collect natural history, conduct experiments, construct and test axioms by induction, and organize scientific labour so as to derive reliable causes and generate new useful works. Emphasises systematic, collective, experiment-first inquiry and precautions against prejudice, sectarianism, and premature speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and test axioms for appropriate scope
rubrics_metrics.description: At in axiomatibus constituendis per hanc inductionem, examinatio et probatio etiam facienda est: utrum quod constituitur axioma aptatum sit tantum et ad mensuram factorum particularium ex quibus extrahitur; an vero sit amplius et latius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you form axioms by induction, explicitly test whether the axiom is merely fitted to the particulars from which it was drawn or whether it claims a wider amplitude. If it is broader, determine whether that breadth can be secured by designating new particulars (a fide-jussione) so the axiom is solid and determinate in matter before applying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use verification by prediction as confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circumstance of a scientific generalisation enabling us to predict the future affords a strong confirmation of its truth, though it does not positively prove it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat successful prediction and the discovery of new particulars implied by an axiom as strong evidence in its favour; design tests that seek newly discoverable instances to strengthen confidence in generalisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidate specialists' results into unified science
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of the labours of specialists require to be gathered together into one science, and the various sciences themselves to be compared and brought into harmony, if human knowledge is to progress as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect, compare and harmonise findings from disparate specialities so that progress is cumulative and provides real insight into nature; avoid fragmentation and truncation of sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer directed, systematic inquiry over chance discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Licet enim semel aut iterum accidere possit, ut quispiam in id forte fortuna incidat… longe plura detegi necesse sit a ratione et industria et directione et intentione hominum, quam a casu et instinctu animalium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organise research by reasoned direction, industry and intention rather than rely on luck or accidental discovery; a systematic method will yield more, better, and quicker results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain a comprehensive natural history (Experientia Literata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historiae Naturalis et Experimentalis collectionem, qualem animo metimur et qualis esse debet, opus esse magnum, et quasi regium, et multae operae atque impensae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a large, carefully organized, and well-funded corpus of natural history and experiments as the indispensable foundation for legitimate interpretation of nature; this is a major undertaking requiring distributed labour and expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive causes and axioms from works and experiments, then derive new works from them
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut non opera ex operibus sive experimenta ex experimentis (ut empirici), sed ex operibus et experimentis causas et axiomata, atque ex causis et axiomatibus rursus nova opera et experimenta (ut legitimi Naturae Interpretes), extrahamus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mere accumulation of isolated empirical recipes; use experiments to infer causes and axioms, and use those causes/axioms to generate new experiments and useful works — an iterative, interpretive methodology rather than simple empiricism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit practical application by mechanicians but prioritise foundational aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Si quis ad mechanica sit magis aptus… ei permittimus et relinquimus illam industriam… Nos vero, cum ad majora contendamus, moram omnem praeproperam et praematuram in istiusmodi rebus damnamus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow craftsmen and mechanicians to extract and apply practical uses from collected history (a temporary benefit), but do not let short-term applications divert the main effort aimed at major, foundational victories over nature; avoid premature haste for minor gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare the mind: remove prejudices and adopt provisional opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequitur ut mens sistatur in positione bona… Valet enim in re nova ad praejudicium, non solum praeoccupatio fortis opinionis veteris, sed et praeceptio sive praefiguratio falsa rei quae affertur… habeantur bonae et verae de iis quae adducimus opiniones, licet ad tempus tantummodo, et tanquam usurariae, donee res ipsa pernoscatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleanse the intellect of idols and biases and adopt a benevolent, open receptive stance; allow provisional (temporary) opinions that serve until the matter itself is fully known — but keep them provisional, not dogmatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and tolerate limited errors in early natural history, but keep them small
rubrics_metrics.description: Multa in historia naturali experimenta falso credi et recipi posse… si in historia naturali et experimentis magna et crebra et continua fuerint errata, ilia nulla ingenii aut artis foelicitate corrigi aut emendari posse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that some mistakes will occur in initial compilations and that isolated errors are correctable when underlying causes and axioms are found; however, ensure rigorous diligence in collection because widespread errors will make correction and progress impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include common and 'vile' phenomena in natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: Sunt enim artium et naturae particularia phaenomena… Homines autem… non morentur contemplationem hominum non morentur… Quod vero ad rerum vilitatem attinet… eae res, non minus quam lautissimae et pretiosissimae in historiam naturalem recipiendae sunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not neglect frequent, low-status, or seemingly trivial phenomena: study the causes of common things thoroughly because philosophers have often ignored them, yet they are essential to discovering important forms and causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disdain sordid or indecorous materials — they can yield high value
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex instantiis vilibus et sordidis quandoque eximia lux et informatio emanat… hoc genus fastidii sit plane puerile et effoeminatum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid aesthetic or moral prejudices that dismiss 'sordid' materials; such materials may produce valuable information and should be included in natural histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for and define 'simplices naturae' (simple natures) as foundational elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicium naturarum cognitionem bene examinatam et definitam instar lucis esse… quando haec 'simple natures' were discovered, it would be easy… to ascertain, through the method of Exclusion, the Form or Cause of any given phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to discover and define the simple elemental natures underlying complex phenomena; these serve as the letters or building blocks from which causes and forms may be determined by exclusion and combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise experiments that produce clear light rather than immediate material use
rubrics_metrics.description: Nos jam sub initiis… tantum hicitfera experimenta, non fructifera quaerere… simplicium naturarum cognitionem bene examinatam… instar lucis esse: quae ad universa operum penetralia aditum prebet… in se tamen non ita magni usus est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At early stages, value experiments that provide conceptual clarity ('light') and access to deeper causes even if they have little immediate practical application; these are seeds for later fruitful operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postpone speculative subtilties until after experimental axioms are constituted
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnem subtilitatem disputationum et discursuum mentis, si adhibebitur tantum post axiomata inventa, seram esse et praeposteram; subtilitatis tempus verum ac proprium versari in pensitanda experientia et inde constituendis axiomatibus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid engaging in speculative verbal subtleties or scholastic hair-splitting before experiments have been done and axioms established; put subtle intellectual analysis after empirical discovery so it grips nature rather than merely words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that some discoveries are unforeseeable but can be anticipated by systematic method
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonnulla ex his quae jam inventa sunt ejus sint generis ut antequam invenirentur haud facile cuiquam in mentem venisset… ita sperandum omnino est esse adhuc in naturae sinu multa excellentis usus recondita… sed per viam, quam nunc tractamus, propere et subito et simul repraesentari et anticipari possunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to the fact that many inventions would not have been imagined beforehand, yet a disciplined method and systematic inquiry can bring such discoveries to light more promptly than chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use division of labour and distribution of tasks to accelerate discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Tum enim homines vires suas nosse incipient, cum non eadem infiniti, sed alia alii praestabunt… Historiae… opus esse magnum… multae operae atque impensae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organise many workers with distributed, complementary tasks so that collective industry and the succession of labour produce inventions and the rapid discovery of causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persevere in trying experiments despite risk and uncertain prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Etiamsi multo infirmior et obscurior aura spei ab ista Nova Continent e spiraverit tamen omnino experiendum esse… Non enim res pari periculo non tentatur, et non succedit; cum in illo ingentis boni, in hoc exiguae humanae operae, jactura vertatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be deterred by uncertain or bleak prospects: undertake experiments even at risk, since the potential gain is enormous relative to the loss of small human effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect to find in collected histories items that seem curious, trivial or overly subtle
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrent etiam in historia nostra… plurimae res, prime leves et vulgatae… postremo nimis subtiles ac mere speculativae… quae genus rerum hominum studia avertere et allenare possit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that a natural history will contain a range from common and trivial items to extremely subtle ones; include them nonetheless because they may be seeds for later theory and are part of a complete empirical base.
